name: Clean Trust
description: Established and trustworthy: navy and blue, with your license and awards out front.
brief:
Aesthetic: mountain blue heritage (Light-ground plumbing sites with blue brand accents, mountain imagery, photo-backed heroes and rounded or pill shapes, grounded by license, award and badge trust marks.)
Vocabulary: mountain photo backdrop, navy photo overlay, pill-shaped buttons, angled hero divider, translucent contact card, uppercase navy H2 headings, italic serif tagline, rounded white feature cards, accreditation and badge band, phone number in sticky nav, checkbox service-area list, dashed coupon card
Reference feel: Everest Plumbing, Greenville SC (everestplumbing.com), Master Service Plumbing, Reno (masterserviceplumbing.com)
House DNA: Phone number on the first mobile screen (9/12); Star-rated reviews on the homepage (7/12); Named list of towns served (7/12); Phone or call button pinned while scrolling (6/12); Trust strip of licenses, ratings and years near the top (6/12); Call is the primary conversion (6/12)
Never: Thin light-blue headings on white, Vague Read More as the only CTA, Faded grey text over busy photos, Muddy grey sections with weak hierarchy, Missing H1 and no lead form, Stray logos floating in white gaps, Phone number below the first mobile screen (3/12 real sites)
One risk: Make the mountain a brand device: a navy-overlaid summit photo behind the hero and reviews, with an angled cut edge and a mid-page call bar with a hand-drawn underline on the phone number.

WORKFLOW - asset first, page second:
Step 1. Generate the hero asset NOW, before any code. Fill [SUBJECT], then Higgsfield gpt_image_2, 16:9, resolution 2k, quality high:
  "16:9 full-bleed photo, 35mm lens at eye level, soft natural daylight, cool navy and teal palette with white highlights. [SUBJECT: plumber's gloved hands tightening copper pipe fittings in a clean utility space, with a faint mountain ridge in the far background]. Subject sits in the right third; the left two-thirds is a darker, smooth navy-toned area for a headline and a single button."
  It must read as a full-bleed hero background (camera inside the scene, edges bleed, negative space held for the headline) - not an isolated 3D asset or product render.
Step 2. Build the page AROUND the real asset - measure its negative space and place typography where the image leaves room.
Everything else: your call. Surprise me.
heroTreatment: Full-bleed crew photo under a navy grade that is deepest behind the copy; an italic serif since-line, a white Montserrat headline, a white booking pill and an outlined call pill; a mountain-ridge edge cuts the photo off at the bottom. Mobile keeps the copy on the photo at a shorter height.
neverList: Thin light-blue headings on white
Vague Read More as the only CTA
Faded grey text over busy photos
Muddy grey sections with weak hierarchy
Missing H1 and no lead form
Stray logos floating in white gaps

name: Bold Local
description: Bold and local: your crew in a big photo, one strong red, and your ratings right on it.
brief:
Aesthetic: red banner plumbers (Clean white pages with a single saturated red or orange accent, darkened full-bleed hero photos, geometric sans headlines and badge-led trust proof.)
Vocabulary: full-bleed darkened photo hero, single saturated red accent, geometric sans headlines, red line-icon service grid, ghost outline hero buttons, red pill phone button, association badge row, stat grid with big numerals, red underline heading accent, black or dark service panel, light grey section panels, dark footer with license details
Reference feel: Lasiter & Lasiter Plumbing, Fort Worth (lasiter.com), Johnson Plumbing, Reno (johnsonplumbingnv.com), Tucson Plumbing, Tucson (tucsonplumbing.com)
House DNA: Phone number on the first mobile screen (9/12); Star-rated reviews on the homepage (7/12); Named list of towns served (7/12); Phone or call button pinned while scrolling (6/12); Trust strip of licenses, ratings and years near the top (6/12); Call is the primary conversion (6/12)
Never: Hero with no headline or call to action, Thin colored subline over a busy photo, Dense small paragraph over hero imagery, Repeating the same stat twice in one view, Claiming reviews without showing any testimonial content, Phone number only in a non-sticky top bar, Phone number below the first mobile screen (3/12 real sites)
One risk: Pair a hero stat grid of big numerals (years, review count, BBB, licensed) beside the headline so the trust bar sits inside the hero photo.

  "16:9 wide photograph, [SUBJECT: branded plumbing van parked in front of a white brick suburban home, or a smiling homeowner at a kitchen faucet], shot at eye level with a 35mm lens in soft overcast daylight, palette of crisp whites, charcoal and one punch of red, darkened tonal grade on the left half, clear negative space on the left third for a headline and buttons, no text or logos."
  It must read as a full-bleed hero background (camera inside the scene, edges bleed, negative space held for the headline) - not an isolated 3D asset or product render.
Step 2. Build the page AROUND the real asset - measure its negative space and place typography where the image leaves room.
Everything else: your call. Surprise me.
heroTreatment: Full-bleed crew photo darkened from the left; a heavy white DM Sans headline, a red booking pill and a ghost outlined call button; the badge and stat trust bar runs across the bottom of the photo. Mobile stacks the trust bar under the copy on the same photo.
neverList: Hero with no headline or call to action
Thin colored subline over a busy photo
Dense small paragraph over hero imagery
Repeating the same stat twice in one view
Claiming reviews without showing any testimonial content
Phone number only in a non-sticky top bar

name: Premium Dark
description: Dark and gold on purpose: none of the 36 contractor sites we studied looks like this, so you will not look like anyone else in town.
brief:
Aesthetic: Dark Mode (OLED) (deep black, dark grey, high contrast, low white emission, visible focus)
Pattern: Trust & Authority + Conversion with a premium register. Hero > Proof > Solution overview > Clear CTA path.
Color strategy: Premium black + gold accent; gold reserved for the call to action and ratings.
Typography: Cormorant / Montserrat (Luxury Serif: elegant heading, geometric body).
Key effects: Minimal glow, dark-to-light transitions (200-300ms), hairline gold rules, no cheap visuals, no fast animations.
Never: Hidden contact info, No certifications, Cheap visuals, Fast animations, Gray-on-gray text, Neon accents.
heroTreatment: Dark page. Copy left with a tall serif headline, a gold booking button and an outlined call button; the crew or trade photo right inside a hairline gold frame with a 0.25 black vignette at the lower edge only, no filter. Mobile: framed photo band on top at a short height, copy below.
neverList: Hidden contact info
No certifications
Cheap visuals
Fast animations
Gray-on-gray text
Neon accents

name: Friendly Family
description: Family-owned and friendly: your crew up front, royal blue panels, and coupons right under the photo.
brief:
Aesthetic: royal blue fleet (Light-ground plumbing sites with saturated royal-blue panels, bold condensed or heavy caps, branded truck and team photo heroes, and card-based service grids.)
Vocabulary: royal blue hero panel, branded truck photo, angled photo cut, condensed caps headlines, icon-suffixed CTA buttons, award badge strip, white service cards on grey, three-column service grid, navy closing band, Google rating pill, coupon or quote cards, dual call and schedule buttons
Reference feel: Gold Seal Plumbing, Spokane (goldsealplumbing.com), Williams Plumbing & Drain, Tulsa (williamsplumbinganddrain.com)
House DNA: Phone number on the first mobile screen (9/12); Star-rated reviews on the homepage (7/12); Named list of towns served (7/12); Phone or call button pinned while scrolling (6/12); Trust strip of licenses, ratings and years near the top (6/12); Call is the primary conversion (6/12)
Never: Thin light-weight body text on white, Tall uneven text-heavy service cards with no relief, Phone number that scrolls away with no sticky header, Service area towns buried in the footer, Dense copy blocks without photos or icons, Small grey review text that hurts legibility, Phone number below the first mobile screen (3/12 real sites)
One risk: Overlap a row of perforated ticket-style coupon cards onto the base of the hero, with a diagonal-cut fleet photo against a solid blue panel.

Subject sits on the right third, left side is clean sky and driveway for a headline. No text or logos."

Phone number that scrolls away with no sticky header
Service area towns buried in the footer

Small grey review text that hurts legibility

name: Modern Minimal
description: Built for the job site: heavy type, black and red, and copy that talks spec and schedule.
brief:
Aesthetic: jobsite red commercial (Full-bleed construction-site photography under dark overlays, flat red buttons, heavy bold sans caps, white icon cards and black bands on a light ground.)
Vocabulary: full-bleed construction photo hero, dark or red gradient overlay, huge white caps headline, flat red CTA buttons, pill or rectangular red buttons, white cards with red line icons, full-black section bands, grayscale badge or logo row, edge-to-edge project photo strip, condensed or heavy grotesk headings, outlined ghost secondary button, full-bleed red feature band
Reference feel: S & K Plumbing of Fort Worth, Fort Worth (skplumbinginc.com), Goodson Plumbing Services, Boise (robgoodsonplumbing.com), All American Plumbing, Tulsa (aapiok.com)
House DNA: Phone number on the first mobile screen (9/12); Star-rated reviews on the homepage (7/12); Named list of towns served (7/12); Phone or call button pinned while scrolling (6/12); Trust strip of licenses, ratings and years near the top (6/12); Call is the primary conversion (6/12)
Never: Thin white headline over a busy unlit photo, Phone number buried small in header only, Muted low-contrast grey trust badges, Repetitive Read More buttons without detail, No quote form or scheduler anywhere, Mixed fonts and colors that feel heavy, Phone number below the first mobile screen (3/12 real sites)
One risk: Cut a black rounded-corner project teaser tab into the bottom of the hero over a red-gradient aerial construction photo, linking straight to project proof.
